title: Anyone see Eileen with Anne Hathaway yet?

commenti.body: Saw it yesterday and loved it. I didn't know anything about the plot I just saw the trailer once. Thought it was absolutely hilarious, super melodramatic and campy. One of my favorites of the year so far.

Recommend going in blind for either the film or the novel. I mean, novels seem to exist solely to eventually be turned into movies these days since it feels like I don’t know anyone who reads anymore. But the novel is also good, if you *do* read.
Wasn't aware it was a novel. I bet it gives a lot more insight to the character of eileen

Yep, by Otessa Mosfegh

I would guess at least 25% of all studio movies and TV shows are adapted from novels at this point. I mean, at least it’s an economic incentive for the novel to stay alive as a medium, which I’ll take.

Just watched it. I really liked it, but it did feel like it ended right when it was hitting it's stride. 

It's like if Parasite ended right after they returned home in the pouring rain. 

Like, it clocks in at 96 minutes. That's so freaking short. It's literally missing a whole 3rd act.

Felt almost like an origin movie, like Eileen was gonna go around the country killing evil people.

Idk, I feel like the movie was an alright length, just the ending montage of visions was a bit sloppy and underwhelming. I feel like Anne Hathaway might have still came to the house too, eileen didn't leave it very long
Not as common as it used to be though. Often books would be published, auctioned and turned into movies all within the same year.
I haven’t read the book but I assume the movie ends where the book does
If you think that you hang out with the wrong people!

I love nothing more than entering a random movie blindly. I just saw Eileen last night and the twist literally gave me whiplash. I'm a simple person. I see Anne Hathaway and I'm ready to see whatever the movie is. This was literally the best "blind" movie I've been seen.
Leave The World Behind is also based on a book, coming out this month

The world of the movie is dreary and unpleasant but I really enjoyed it. I went in expecting a companion piece to *Carol*, which I guess it could be, and was completely blindsided by the twist in the most amazing way. 

It's also very well acted and the climax is oof. And Anne Hathaway's character is already a camp icon in my mind.

Great movie. The direction was like a 70s movie. Great performance from the kid prisoners mom. All around great movie. 

I for one am a fan of the runtime. My only criticism is the beginning could’ve moved faster to have a more depraved third act.
